initialBefore.instrumentation: Canvas/bounds wrappers and rAF observation; method timing includes own microtiming overhead; full Chrome trace enabled only final phase. Mouse input comes from Playwright isolated headless browser. Observed latency includes wait until the next rAF sees committed dataset frameSeq and is an upper bound on commit latency. CPU/RSS is own Chrome process tree from CDP, excluding CEF/Node and other host processes. GIF remains active in stationary phase.

validation: Private Node24 server/client TypeScript and Vite builds passed.
Actual production same-N PNG, old-N object deletion/reload, two cancellation timing cases and same-URL service restart passed.
Chrome DPR1/2 generic and trusted scene tests passed with 72 complete layers, stale N rejection, immutable copied pixels, taint/type/draw/dimension errors preserving previous visible pixels.
Seven actual production material kinds including CEF HTML at DPR2 each compared PNG channels with zero mismatches.
Actual CSS-origin, CSS page zoom, native focus/scroll, point binding and narrow layout passed.

Independent renderer post-fix checks: eleven CanvasPattern paint fields rejected, six other failures preserve pixels/metadata, four generic/trusted raster equivalence groups and retained PNG after six scratch reuses/resize passed.
Final default suite remains assigned to the delivery executor after source cutoff.
limitations: Short instrumented Chrome runs on the same host; Canvas wrappers, geometry matching and registry counters add measurement cost. CPU/RSS covers only owned Chrome processes, not service/CEF/other host processes; summed RSS can count shared pages.
Commit latency is input-to-matching visible Canvas draw, excluding compositor display delay. The first sub-threshold move is omitted, giving 59 matching drag/pan inputs per 60 generated moves.

PositionMatchedBefore includes stationary and later active/trace phases; final repetitions use only drag/pan after the same initial fixture readiness and 1-second warmup. Extra before stationary warmup is explicit.
GIF continues animating in stationary/static-HTML phases. HTML/native-source PNG polling remains at its existing rate.

Full Chrome timeline tracing is enabled only for the active final trace phase in full runs; the final two focused drag/pan runs have no full interaction trace. Overlapping trace durations cannot be summed as wall time.
Initial rAF-based latency in the earliest raw before/intermediate runs can pair with unrelated producer frames and is preserved as historical measurement only.
The first staging after run had genuine pan tail stalls and is retained; producer CPU-readback contexts plus stable Markdown DOM address the measured cause.
Firefox was unavailable; its original failed launch and partial Chromium traces are retained. No physical Safari/trackpad acceptance is claimed.
sourceChanges: Coalesced browser animation-frame invalidation; comment mutations only.
Renderer-owned persistent staging and same-size visible Canvas reuse.
Trusted primitive runtime string/finite-number validation; copied private texture brand.
Immutable content and controlled-panel Canvas contexts declare willReadFrequently; existing origin checks retained.
Markdown HTML prop remains stable for the same actual text, preserving DOM and avoiding mutation repaint.
Authenticated view presence before native source activation; typed owner retirement and bounded reconnect.
Input ownership reset on page/source lifecycle; synchronous accumulated wheel fields and dedicated touch/native paths.
